gloss: from far away, all the way

definitions.gloss: from far away, all the way, over a great distance
definitions.explanation: Emphasizes that someone has traveled or something has come from a great distance. Conveys a sense of effort or impressiveness in the journey.

examples.japanese: はるばる{来|き}てくれた。
examples.english: You came all the way here.

examples.japanese: {北海道|ほっかいどう}からはるばる{会|あ}いに{来|き}た。
examples.english: I came all the way from Hokkaido to see you.

examples.japanese: はるばる{海|うみ}を{渡|わた}って{届|とど}いた{手紙|てがみ}を{大切|たいせつ}に{読|よ}んだ。
examples.english: I carefully read the letter that had come all the way across the sea.

notes:
KANJI NOTE:
Can be written as {遥々|はるばる} or {遙々|はるばる}, but the hiragana form is most common.

USAGE:
Typically followed by verbs of movement: {来|く}る, {行|い}く, {訪|たず}ねる, {旅|たび}する, etc.
Often implies appreciation or admiration for the effort of the journey.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- はるばる{来|き}てくれる: to come all the way (with gratitude)
- はるばる{出|で}かける: to set out on a long journey
- はるばる{海|うみ}を{渡|わた}る: to cross the sea from afar
